items.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Until Dorothy Mendelsohn, around 12 years old, piqued my interest in piano playing, I thought of math, I thought of science.

ctx.x: What about your academic career? Were you a good student? And what subjects were you interested in?

Until Dorothy Mendelsohn, around 12 years old, piqued my interest in piano playing, I thought of math, I thought of science. Fortunately, before I had to decide, make a decision, Dorothy Mendelsohn came into my life, and it became music. My grades were average. I wasn’t an exceptional student at all, as I recall. I recall teachers saying, “Ramsey, you got to get your homework in,” those kinds of things. I don’t ever recall anybody saying, you’re on the honor roll.
